tasks.title: Restore Add phase and zero-phase recovery
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A roadmap without phases cannot be structurally recovered in the current workspace.

**Finding**
Phase creation and zero-phase recovery were absent from the workspace.

**Scope**
Add one canonical phase factory/mutation; wire visible toolbar, zero-state, and end-of-list creation actions; respect owner/editor/viewer modes; persist local and synced edits; record activity; focus the new phase.

**Acceptance criteria**
A zero-phase owner/editor can create a phase by keyboard, pointer, and touch; viewers get an explanatory read-only state; new phase survives reload/sync and creates one attributed activity event.

**Validation / gate**
Unit and component tests for factory/mutation/permissions/focus; browser smoke for local and synced paths; regression test deleting the final phase then recovering.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. Factory, mutation, zero/filtered/viewer states, visible native-button actions, duplicate activation protection, expansion, focused naming, local write-through, aggregate autosync wiring, and `phase.created` activity are implemented. Four focused test files pass with 14 tests; lint and typecheck pass. Browser smoke now proves pointer creation, focus on the new phase name, reload persistence, and final-phase deletion recovery, and the owner/editor/viewer control matrix. Remaining gate: a real two-session synced session confirming save and one attributed `phase.created` activity event, plus touch activation on a real device. Both are covered by manual QA sections 25b and 33.

**Risk**
Without this, destructive phase deletion can strand an editable roadmap.

**Evidence**
`roadmap-factory.ts`, `usePhaseMutations.ts`, `usePhaseCollapse.ts`, `Workspace`, `WorkspaceToolbar`, `PhaseList`, `PhaseNameEditor`, activity display/count handling, and focused RF-016 tests.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Make phase settings and color overlays viewport-safe
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A structural action must remain usable at narrow widths and zoom.

**Finding**
The phase menu and color controls previously used clipped in-tree absolute overlays without collision or focus management.

**Scope**
Adopt a small shared anchored-menu/popover foundation only where it replaces this duplicated behavior; migrate phase settings/color first and define layering/scroll ownership.

**Acceptance criteria**
Menu and popover remain within viewport at narrow desktop, mobile, and 200% zoom; Escape/outside click work; trigger regains focus; keyboard semantics and focus order are correct.

**Validation / gate**
Component tests plus browser screenshots/interaction smoke at narrow viewport and 200% zoom; manual screen-reader check.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. `AnchoredOverlay` portals fixed-position content, flips and clamps to the viewport, limits height, repositions on resize/scroll/content changes, and owns outside/Escape dismissal, initial focus, focus return, menu arrow/Home/End navigation, and dialog Tab trapping. Phase settings and color controls use the primitive, mobile/touch triggers remain visible, layer order is tokenized, card overflow workarounds are removed, and custom color state follows the active phase. Ten focused interaction/position tests pass; lint and typecheck pass. Remaining gate: browser screenshots and interaction smoke at narrow viewport/mobile/200% zoom plus a manual screen-reader semantics check.

**Risk**
Overlay regressions can clip structural actions or make keyboard users lose context.

**Evidence**
`AnchoredOverlay`, anchored-overlay CSS and layer token, `PhaseSettingsMenu`, `Phase`, `phase.css`, and focused overlay/menu tests.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Make phase mutation persistence and activity consistent
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Participants need truthful, useful history for structural changes.

**Finding**
Create was the only fully attributed structural phase mutation; other phase changes were missing events or used legacy reorder vocabulary, and an edit landing during an in-flight autosync could retain acknowledged activity or miss its retry.

**Scope**
Define canonical phase mutation/activity vocabulary and no-op rules; make local/synced persistence and attribution consistent without duplicate events.

**Acceptance criteria**
Create, rename, delete, reorder, color, and color-mode each produce at most one useful activity event when changed and none for no-ops; synced save retains the events.

**Validation / gate**
Focused mutation/activity tests and two-session manual check.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. Phase mutations emit `phase.created`, `phase.updated`, `phase.deleted`, or `phase.reordered` with useful field and phase metadata; unchanged, missing, duplicate, and malformed operations emit nothing. Pending activity now acknowledges only the object references captured by a successful request, preserves newer edits, and retries a debounce blocked by an in-flight save. Activity labels and batch counts cover the canonical vocabulary while legacy reorder display remains compatible. Twenty-five focused frontend tests pass; lint and typecheck pass. The database-backed API regression now runs against the repository test PostgreSQL service and passes as part of 236 API tests. Remaining gate: verify attribution, save, and realtime refresh in the manual two-session check, section 25b.

**Risk**
Missing or duplicate structural history undermines collaboration recovery.

**Evidence**
`usePhaseMutations.ts`, `activity-changes.ts`, `useAutoSync.ts`, `useSaveFlow.ts`, `ActivityPanel.tsx`, and focused web/API regressions.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Protect destructive final-phase and empty-workspace paths
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Destructive actions must never leave an editor without a recovery route.

**Finding**
Recovery actions existed after phase creation work, but the delete confirmation did not identify the final-phase recovery path, viewer empty phases did not explain task restrictions, and menu-to-dialog focus could land on the dialog container instead of the safe action.

**Scope**
Specify final-phase confirmation/recovery, empty-phase first-task action, filtered-empty action, and owner/editor/viewer copy.

**Acceptance criteria**
Every editable empty state has a relevant action; every viewer state explains why editing is unavailable; final-phase deletion has an immediate recovery path.

**Validation / gate**
Component tests for empty states and browser smoke across roles.

**Implementation status**
Complete. Delete confirmation accurately reports top-level tasks and subtasks, identifies final-phase deletion, and names Create first phase as the recovery action. Its menu-to-alertdialog handoff reliably focuses Keep phase; buttons have explicit non-submit types and Escape remains safe. Empty phases expose Add first task to editors and explain the viewer restriction; zero-phase and filtered-empty states retain distinct create/reset actions based on the unfiltered roadmap phase count. Twenty-nine focused interaction and accessibility tests pass within a 450-test web suite, alongside lint, typecheck, and production build. The stated browser gate is met: the smoke suite exercises owner, editor, and viewer states and walks final-phase deletion through to recovery. The API gate that was previously environment-blocked now passes with 236 tests against isolated PostgreSQL.

**Risk**
A recoverability failure is a Beta blocker even if data deletion is confirmed.

**Evidence**
`PhaseSettingsMenu`, `ConfirmDialog`, `PhaseEmptyState`, `PhaseList`, `Workspace`, and focused empty/destructive-state tests.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Establish a visible primary-action hierarchy
tasks.desc:

**Scope**

**Acceptance criteria**
Phase/task creation is discoverable in editable views; secondary actions remain keyboard/touch accessible; read-only action labels remain truthful.

**Validation / gate**

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. The action matrix covers local, owner/editor, and viewer states. Add phase remains the first emphasized action in Roadmap view and stays available from Team view, while contextual search/filter/tag/expansion controls remain Roadmap-only. Empty/filter states keep task-specific recovery, no-op expansion controls are hidden, local Activity is focusable with a visible after-save explanation, mobile Add phase owns a full row, and rename/settings/reorder affordances retain visible low-emphasis defaults without hover. Twenty-three focused role, interaction, and accessibility tests pass; lint and typecheck pass. Browser coverage now spans desktop, a 390 CSS-pixel mobile viewport, a 640 CSS-pixel 200% reflow proxy, coarse-pointer affordance visibility, and 36px-or-larger critical mobile targets, with no horizontal overflow. Remaining gate: real 200% browser zoom and a real touch device, covered by manual QA section 33.

tasks.title: Truthful save, error, offline, and session recovery states
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Users must distinguish local save, server sync, validation, conflict, and expired session outcomes.

**Finding**
Typed classification existed, but queued server edits reported Live during debounce, validation and unexpected failures had no stable attention state, connectivity could fail silently in autosync, and some forbidden paths revoked a valid session as if it had expired.

**Scope**
Map save states and messages across local and server roadmaps; preserve drafts; remove generic/misleading errors; document deliberate limitations.

**Acceptance criteria**
No network condition is described as synced incorrectly; validation differs from connectivity; retry/reload/keep-local outcomes preserve user input.

**Validation / gate**
Focused hook tests and manual fault-injection browser matrix.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. Server-backed unsaved work reports Saving during debounce/in-flight work; validation, permission, and unexpected failures report Save needs attention; connection failures report Offline; conflicts remain distinct; and only expired/unauthorized sessions clear credentials. Autosync, manual save/reload/keep-local, and task patch flows provide outcome-specific messages and explicitly preserve local edits or task drafts. Retry/review actions remain available, newer in-flight edits remain queued, and existing idle-render/caret tests cover stable typing. Twenty-nine focused save, error, task-draft, and caret tests pass; lint and typecheck pass. Remaining gate: manual browser fault injection for connection loss/recovery, validation, 403, expiry, conflict reload, and keep-local across local and synced sessions.

**Risk**
Incorrect status can cause accidental loss or false confidence.

**Evidence**
`roadmap-sync-errors`, `useAutoSync`, `useSaveFlow`, `useTaskPatch`, sync status/indicator/header components, and controlled failure tests.

**Classification**

**Scope**

**Acceptance criteria**

**Risk**

**Evidence**

**Implementation status**

Running those assertions against a real database for the first time exposed three over-strict comparisons that compared responses to request payloads; the API deliberately echoes unset optional tag fields as null, and the assertions now match that contract. Restore behaviour itself was correct. Remaining gate: the manual import/export compatibility check against a real historical or user-supplied file.

**Classification**
confirmed

**Acceptance criteria**
A first-time user can find where data lives, create phase/task, export, save/share, understand roles/locks/conflicts, restore a version, and report a problem. Selecting the RoadForge template deep-clones the canonical JSON into an independent roadmap, resets runtime/export metadata, preserves its registered tags, and cannot mutate the source through user editing. No separately maintained hard-coded roadmap can drift. CI validates the canonical file through RoadForge's real parser and strict template invariants. Template selection has component and browser regression coverage.

**Validation / gate**

**Implementation status**

The RF-033 browser smoke now creates a roadmap from the bundled template and confirms its content renders. Remaining gate: the user's first-run usability walkthrough.

Hover-only subtask/dependency actions become visible on focus and coarse pointers. Phase, task, and subtask ordering is drag-only: editable rows retain pointer, touch, and dnd-kit Space → Arrow → Space keyboard drag handles, while duplicate Move earlier/later/up/down buttons and their empty layout slots are absent. Every `DndContext` has a deterministic semantic ID, and a production-browser regression checks console and page errors before navigation, across template expansion, Roadmap/Tags switching, reload, and blank-roadmap creation. Tags is a proper workspace tab for local, owner, editor, and viewer roadmaps; task search/filter tools remain Roadmap-only, and the Tags panel and task metadata share one color-safe tag-chip component.

**Automated evidence**
Focused component and Chromium regressions cover axe scans, initial focus, Escape and focus return, zero rendered phase/task/subtask move actions, pointer drag plus reload persistence and contiguous numbering, viewer restrictions, disclosure preservation, deterministic drag descriptions, tab keyboard semantics, tag usage and mutation states, reduced motion, critical mobile targets, responsive Roadmap/Activity/Tags navigation, and horizontal overflow. The production-build hydration regression fails on hydration, DndDescribedBy, page, or unclassified console errors. The axe gate previously found and fixed insufficient contrast in the local Activity availability explanation.

**Manual remainder**
Run section 33 with NVDA plus Firefox or Chrome and VoiceOver plus Safari, including landmarks, wizard step changes, phase/task operations, drag-handle announcements, live announcements, 200% zoom, mobile screen reader, and reduced motion.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Measure large-roadmap performance and sync payload limits
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Planning workflows need reproducible scale evidence before optimization or Beta release decisions.

**Implemented**
Added parser-valid small, medium, and large fixtures with 50, 250, and 1,000 tasks. `benchmark:roadmap` runs median CPU budgets, existing typing/caret and render-subscription regressions, controlled autosync/realtime tests, then a one-worker production Chromium benchmark. The browser stage builds and serves the same `output: 'standalone'` artifact the Dockerfile ships via `scripts/serve-standalone.mjs`, so a passing run also proves the deployable server boots. `docs/performance.md` defines commands, fixture content, budgets, the recorded baseline, sync/import boundaries, and deployed limitations.

**Measured baseline**
Verified 2026-07-25 on one Linux workstation. The 1,000-task autosync request is 297.0 KiB against a 384 KiB budget and 512 KiB API ceiling. Median CPU results: hydration preparation 27.5 ms, cache round trip 2.0 ms, broad filter 1.5 ms, display-number preparation 0.5 ms, parser import 2.9 ms, JSON export 9.3 ms, and Markdown export 8.8 ms. Production Chromium: hydration to usable 628.6 ms, controlled middle-string typing/caret 80.8 ms, broad search stabilization 1,764.1 ms, and 50-task phase expansion 435.1 ms.

**Result**
All budgets pass. Browser timings vary widely between runs on the same machine, so a single run is not a baseline; across five consecutive runs hydration measured 629-947 ms, typing/caret 48-185 ms, search 1,350-1,764 ms, and phase expansion 262-435 ms. Broad search has far less headroom than any other metric, with its worst observed run about 12% below budget while every other metric stayed several times clear. It is deliberately not exempted or loosened, because a gate that only just passes is the useful early warning. Input node identity and caret position remain stable; unchanged PhaseList props do not rerender children; controlled autosync and realtime state tests pass. No speculative optimization was introduced. Real browser diversity, storage quotas, PostgreSQL/Redis latency, proxy limits, and cross-worker propagation remain RF-023/RF-036 deployment evidence.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Execute security, backup, and deployment proof gates
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Code and documentation cannot substitute for operational proof.

**Finding**
CI includes audits and migration checks and self-hosting docs prescribe backup/restore, but no evidence proved a deployed candidate, restore drill, rollback, or monitored smoke. The dependency gate had also gone stale: `make audit` and the CI `js-audit` job were failing with twelve advisories, six high, all reaching production through `next@15.5.18`.

**Implemented**
Upgraded `next` and `eslint-config-next` to 15.5.21 and added `pnpm.overrides` raising `postcss` to ^8.5.23 and `sharp` to ^0.35.3, which Next still pins at vulnerable versions. `make audit` and `pip-audit` now both report no known vulnerabilities. `docs/security/dependency-audit-policy.md` records each override with its removal condition. Added `docs/security/operational-proof-gate.md`, which classifies every RF-036 check as automated, local manual, deployed manual, or decision, and gives each remaining check exact prerequisites, command, expected output, pass/fail criterion, and evidence to retain.

**Automated evidence**
236 API tests pass against isolated PostgreSQL, covering minimal health response and security headers, credential-free access logs, docs disabled outside development, production secret-key and database-URL guards, memory-mode multi-worker rejection, Redis URL requirement and startup ping, trusted-proxy and forwarded-header handling, body-size limits, rate limits, and role/share-link/session enforcement. `make api-check` reports no migration drift. Secret, tracked-artifact, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` scans are clean: only `.env.example` files are tracked, no build output is tracked, and the single public variable is `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.

**Local manual evidence**
Rehearsed the documented backup and disposable restore drill end to end against local disposable data: dump written and non-empty, catalog readable, checksum verified, drill database created, restore completed with `--exit-on-error`, verification counts matched, drill database dropped. Live checks against the local stack confirmed the minimal health response with all four security headers and CORS echoing an allowed origin while rejecting a disallowed one with no allow-origin header.

**Deployed remainder**
Section 3 of the proof gate remains open and cannot be settled locally: HTTPS/HSTS at the edge, trusted-proxy client IPs, credential-safe proxy and application log review, share-link and session revocation, rate limiting under the real proxy, pre-migration backup plus upgrade and drift check, projection backfill parity, worker/realtime mode confirmation, two-session collaboration, and rollback rehearsal.

**Risk**
Operational failures are high impact and cannot be inferred locally. The dependency overrides are a version floor, not a suppression, and must be rechecked on every Next upgrade.

**Classification**
confirmed

**Updated collaboration remainder**
The deployed proof must now also verify immediate realtime revocation, conflict-safe restore, privileged invite handling, automatic reconnect/replay, Redis outage recovery, presence accuracy, hidden-tab notification badges, multi-worker convergence, and privacy-safe collaboration metrics.

tasks.title: Promote Tags to a first-class workspace tab with drag ordering
tasks.desc:
**Delivered capability**
Tags are a first-class Roadmap / Activity / Tags workspace tab. Registry rows use the canonical task tag chip, show usage counts, support owner/editor mutations, remain read-only for viewers, and reorder through deterministic dnd-kit drag-and-drop rather than move-arrow controls.

**Evidence**
Shared tag-chip rendering, Tags panel/tab semantics, deterministic drag context IDs, pointer and keyboard drag coverage, persistence/reload coverage, hydration regression coverage, and responsive browser tests.

**Boundary**
This records the delivered UI capability; collaboration presence and realtime durability are planned separately.

tasks.title: Unify tag and phase color controls and editor styling
tasks.desc:
**Delivered capability**
Tag editing uses the same normalized input, focus treatment, anchored palette, color validation, custom-color entry, and crisp circular swatch language as phase color editing. Duplicate focus rings and pixelated native color-well presentation were removed.

**Evidence**
Shared color-picker and swatch ownership, shared palette/validation tests, focus and cancellation coverage, responsive popover checks, and persistence after reload.

**Boundary**
No roadmap schema or backend API change was required.

tasks.title: Preserve safe legacy tag identifiers across save and restore
tasks.desc:
**Delivered capability**
RoadForge accepts safe historical tag identifiers such as `status:done` and `priority:P0` while continuing to generate strict lowercase-kebab IDs for new tags. Existing IDs and task references are preserved byte-for-byte across load, save, version, restore, export, and import.

**Evidence**
Frontend/backend contract tests, legacy roadmap fixtures, database-backed save/checkpoint/restore coverage, browser refresh regression, and no silent ID migration.

**Boundary**
The compatibility grammar remains deliberately narrow and continues rejecting spaces, paths, control characters, markup, and malformed separators.

tasks.title: Cut off revoked participants from realtime immediately
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Revocation must remove both mutation rights and passive live visibility.

**Finding**
REST authorization checks `revoked_at`, but an already-open SSE stream can continue receiving roadmap and lock events until disconnect or session expiry.

**Scope**
Add server-side stream revocation enforcement, publish a revocation control event, close matching connections across memory and Redis backends, clear client credentials, and stop reconnect attempts for revoked sessions.

**Acceptance criteria**
Revocation closes every active tab for that participant promptly; no later realtime event is delivered; subsequent reads and writes fail; other participants remain connected; the behavior works in one-worker and Redis multi-worker modes.

**Validation / gate**
API/event-bus tests, an open-stream revocation integration test, two-browser browser coverage, and deployed multi-worker proof.

**Risk**
A revoked collaborator retaining live read access breaks the trust meaning of revocation.

**Evidence**
The collaboration audit confirmed that `event_bus.stream()` does not re-check participant revocation after ticket redemption.

**Classification**
confirmed P1; sole next task.

**Implementation evidence (2026-07-26)**
Backend: participant-scoped SSE stream closure added in `event_bus.py` — `MemoryEventBus`/`RedisPubSubEventBus.stream()` now accept `participant_id` and close the connection the moment they forward a `participant.revoked` event targeting that participant; both backends also poll an injected `is_still_authorized` check once per idle heartbeat as defense-in-depth. `GET /events` (`roadmaps.py`) re-checks `is_participant_revoked()` before opening the stream (closes the ticket-issued-then-revoked race) and wires the heartbeat revalidator through a fresh short-lived DB session. Existing REST-401-on-revoke, ticket-denial-on-revoke, and owner-cannot-revoke-self (400) behavior confirmed already correct and unchanged; frontend revocation teardown (`useRoadmapRealtime.ts` `handleAccessLoss`) already existed and is unchanged.

Automated tests (passing): unit-level MemoryEventBus/RedisPubSubEventBus closure-on-own-revocation, no-closure-for-other-participant, heartbeat-revalidation-closes-stream; HTTP-level ticket-issued-then-revoked-then-redeemed returns 401, revoked participant cannot request a new ticket, `is_participant_revoked` helper coverage; existing revoked-session-401 and revoke-publishes-SSE-event tests re-verified passing.

**Remaining gates (manual/deployed, not automatable here)**
Two-browser live coverage of "revoke closes an already-open tab within seconds" and deployed Redis multi-worker proof, per this task's own validation/gate. An HTTP-level test attempting to assert the open-stream closure end-to-end was written and discarded: httpx's ASGI transport in this harness cannot bound the client-side read independently of the server-side generator, making that specific test either racy or silently dependent on the heartbeat fallback rather than the immediate path. The immediate and fallback paths are instead verified directly at the event-bus level, which is the exact code the route delegates to.

tasks.title: Make version restore conflict-safe
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A restore must not silently replace work saved after the owner opened the Versions panel.

**Finding**
Normal PUT/PATCH writes use optimistic concurrency, but version restore writes the stored snapshot directly without checking the caller's base revision.

**Scope**
Require `expected_updated_at`, route restore through the canonical compare-and-swap conflict contract, checkpoint the pre-restore state, expose 409 metadata to the existing conflict UI, and provide a separately confirmed owner force-restore path only after review.

**Acceptance criteria**
A stale restore returns 409 and changes nothing; a current restore succeeds; an explicit forced restore records actor, source version, overwritten revision, and safety checkpoint; unsaved local drafts receive a specific warning.

**Validation / gate**
Backend concurrency tests, owner UI tests, two-browser restore-versus-edit test, and version round-trip coverage.

**Risk**
The current path can overwrite another collaborator's recently saved work without warning.

**Classification**
confirmed P1.

**Implementation evidence (2026-07-26)**
Backend: `POST /versions/{id}/restore` now requires `last_updated_at` (+ optional `force`) and routes through the same compare-and-swap contract as PUT/PATCH (`version_service.restore_roadmap_version`): a stale base returns the canonical 409 `roadmap_conflict` response and writes nothing; a current base restores normally; an explicit `force=true` (owner-only, enforced by the existing `_OWNER_ONLY` role gate) bypasses the check and records `force`/`overwritten_updated_at` in the restore's activity/version metadata. Every restore — forced or not — now creates an unconditional pre-restore safety-checkpoint version of the current state before mutating, so a restore is always recoverable.

Frontend: `restoreRoadmapVersion()` sends `last_updated_at`/`force`; `VersionsPanel` warns about unsaved local changes before restoring, shows a dedicated conflict confirmation (not a generic failure toast) on 409 carrying the fresh server name/revision, and offers an owner-only "Force restore anyway" action from that dialog.

Automated tests (passing): stale restore returns 409 and changes nothing (no misleading version/activity entries); current-base restore succeeds; force restore overwrites and records `force`/`overwritten_updated_at`; editor cannot force restore (403); pre-restore safety checkpoint created and independently fetchable; all pre-existing restore/version/tag-registry/projection-parity tests updated for the new request contract and re-verified passing. Frontend `VersionsPanel` tests cover current-base restore, the conflict dialog replacing the generic toast, and force restore from that dialog.

**Remaining gates (manual/deployed, not automatable here)**
Two-browser "concurrent editor save vs owner restore" live test, per this task's own validation/gate.

tasks.title: Harden owner and editor invitation credentials
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Privileged invitations are credentials and should not behave like ordinary public hyperlinks.

**Finding**
Owner/editor invitations are rendered as complete join URLs that can leak through history, link previews, Safe Links scanners, or accidental navigation.

**Scope**
Use copy-only/reveal-on-demand presentation for privileged invites, preserve a convenient viewer-link flow, display role/expiry/revocation state, prevent automatic anchor navigation, and evaluate one-time redemption without weakening accountless sharing.

**Acceptance criteria**
Privileged credentials are never rendered as auto-navigable anchors; copying is explicit; rotation/revocation invalidates prior credentials; logs, analytics, referrers, and previews do not receive tokens; viewer sharing remains understandable.

**Validation / gate**
Component/security tests, token-leak scans, join/rotation regression tests, and manual Slack/email preview review using disposable credentials.

**Risk**
A leaked editor or owner invitation grants durable elevated access.

**Classification**
confirmed P1/security.

tasks.title: Enforce production collaboration security configuration
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Production must fail safely when collaboration-facing security configuration is contradictory.

**Finding**
Existing startup guards cover secrets, database URLs, workers, and Redis, but no equivalent fail-fast rule prevents wildcard CORS with credentials.

**Scope**
Reject unsafe production CORS combinations, document the bearer-token/no-cookie CSRF model, retain query-string redaction for SSE tickets, and test security headers, trusted proxies, body limits, and access-log sanitization together.

**Acceptance criteria**
Unsafe production configuration refuses startup with actionable diagnostics; valid explicit origins work; wildcard-plus-credentials cannot deploy; no token or ticket reaches logs.

**Validation / gate**
Configuration unit tests, production-startup smoke, proxy/header tests, and deployed edge verification.

**Risk**
Misconfiguration can undermine otherwise correct route authorization.

**Classification**
confirmed defense-in-depth.

**Implementation evidence (2026-07-26)**
`Settings.validate_startup_security()` now also rejects, in production-like environments, an empty `ROADFORGE_CORS_ORIGINS`, any empty/malformed entry, and the wildcard `*` — the API always sets `allow_credentials=True` (bearer tokens/SSE tickets, never cookies), so wildcard-plus-credentials must never reach a deployment. Documented the bearer-token/no-cookie CSRF model and the new guard in `docs/public-deployment-security.md`. Query-string log redaction, security headers, trusted-proxy handling, body limits, and Redis/worker fail-fast checks were audited and confirmed already correct and already tested; no changes needed there.

Automated tests (passing): wildcard+credentials rejected, empty origins rejected, malformed origin entries rejected (parametrized), explicit multi-origin config accepted; allowed-Origin request receives matching `access-control-allow-origin`/`allow-credentials`; disallowed Origin receives no CORS headers; all pre-existing production-startup, header, trusted-proxy, and access-log-redaction tests re-verified passing.

**Remaining gates (manual/deployed, not automatable here)**
Deployed edge/reverse-proxy verification, per this task's own validation/gate.

tasks.title: Add automatic SSE reconnect and visible connection states
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A dropped live connection must heal without a tab visibility change or manual refresh.

**Finding**
The client sets `reconnecting` after an SSE error but does not run a normal retry loop.

**Scope**
Implement exponential backoff with jitter, bounded retry intervals, fresh single-use ticket acquisition per attempt, cancellation on unmount/revocation, online/visibility acceleration, and persistent Live / Reconnecting / Offline / Resyncing UI states.

**Acceptance criteria**
Transient disconnects reconnect automatically; long outages remain truthful; only one connection attempt runs at a time; revocation and session expiry stop retry; successful reconnect triggers authoritative synchronization.

**Validation / gate**
Fake-timer hook tests, browser network interruption tests, server restart test, and accessible status announcements.

**Classification**
confirmed P1.

**Implementation evidence (2026-07-26)**
`useRoadmapRealtime.ts` now runs a real reconnect loop instead of a status flag with no retry: transient failures (ticket/lock fetch errors, EventSource `onerror`) schedule a retry with exponential backoff and full jitter over the top half of each range, capped at 30s (`lib/reconnect-backoff.ts`), fetch a brand-new single-use ticket on every attempt, never run concurrently, and are accelerated immediately (bypassing remaining backoff) by `window` `online` events or the tab becoming visible. Every connect and reconnect now gates the `live` transition on one authoritative `getRoadmap()` refetch (new `updating`/resync step) rather than the SSE handshake alone; a failed refetch remains `reconnecting`/`offline` instead of falsely reporting live, and local unsaved drafts are preserved through both the periodic `roadmap.updated` handler and the post-reconnect resync. Revocation, roadmap deletion, session expiry, or any definitive 401/403 permanently stop the retry loop and surface a new `access-lost` connection/workspace-status state in addition to the existing revoked-session toast. All timers and the EventSource are cancelled on unmount or roadmap/session change.

Automated tests (passing): exponential/jitter/cap math; hook-level fake-timer coverage of resync-before-live, no-concurrent-connections, fresh-ticket-per-retry, online-event acceleration, revocation permanently stopping retries, a failed post-reconnect resync staying truthful while preserving the local draft, and timer/subscription cancellation on unmount. The existing `role="status" aria-live="polite"` status region already avoided per-heartbeat announcements and required no change.

**Remaining gates (manual/deployed, not automatable here)**
Real Playwright browser network-interruption test and a live server-restart reconnect test, per this task's own validation/gate.

tasks.title: Add realtime event IDs, sequencing, deduplication, and gap detection
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Clients need to know whether an event is new, duplicated, delayed, or missing.

**Finding**
Current events carry no unique ID or per-roadmap sequence, so delivery gaps and duplicate/out-of-order events cannot be detected.

**Scope**
Define a versioned event envelope with event ID, roadmap ID, monotonic sequence, type, actor/session metadata, emitted timestamp, and minimal payload; emit SSE `id:` fields; persist the last applied sequence client-side per active roadmap; ignore duplicates and detect gaps.

**Acceptance criteria**
Events apply once and in order; duplicates are harmless; stale events are ignored; a sequence gap enters Resyncing and fetches the authoritative snapshot; own writes do not produce misleading remote-update notifications.

**Validation / gate**
Envelope contract tests, duplicate/delay/reorder tests, browser reload tests, and compatibility handling for pre-sequence events during deployment.

**Risk**
Bad sequencing can create false freshness or repeated UI updates.

**Classification**
confirmed architecture gap.

tasks.title: Provide a short realtime replay window and authoritative resync
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A brief network drop or rolling restart should not silently discard every event.

**Finding**
The current pub/sub stream has no replay buffer; missed events are recoverable only through an implicit full refetch.

**Scope**
Add a bounded per-roadmap event buffer using a Redis Stream or equivalent durable short-TTL structure, with an in-memory ring buffer for one-worker development. Support reconnect from `Last-Event-ID` when available and fall back to snapshot resync when history has expired.

**Acceptance criteria**
Short disconnects replay missed events in order; expired or invalid cursors trigger one safe snapshot refresh; replay is bounded by count/TTL; revoked sessions cannot replay; deployment remains compatible across rolling versions.

**Validation / gate**
Memory/Redis contract suite, reconnect/replay integration tests, rolling-restart simulation, and payload/retention budgets.

**Risk**
An unbounded event log creates privacy and storage liabilities.

**Classification**
recommended reliability foundation.

tasks.title: Recover safely from Redis runtime outages
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A runtime Redis interruption must not leave workers permanently divergent after Redis returns.

**Finding**
Startup fail-fast behavior is strong, but runtime publish/subscription failures have no proven reconnect and cross-worker reconciliation path.

**Scope**
Add Redis connection retry/backoff, subscription re-establishment, explicit degraded state, health/readiness signals, sequence-gap resync after recovery, and clear fail-closed behavior for multi-worker realtime operations.

**Acceptance criteria**
Redis loss is detected and surfaced; subscriptions recover automatically; clients resync after recovery; no worker silently reports Live while cross-worker delivery is unavailable; one-worker memory mode remains unaffected.

**Validation / gate**
Disposable Redis outage/restart tests, two-worker integration, readiness checks, and structured failure logs.

**Classification**
likely P1 in multi-worker deployments.

phases.name: Presence, activity awareness, and update notifications

tasks.title: Create an ephemeral multi-worker presence model
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Teams need to know who currently has the roadmap open without turning presence into durable audit data.

**Finding**
The Team panel exposes `lastSeenAt`, but there is no realtime online/viewing model and each worker only knows its own SSE subscribers.

**Scope**
Define ephemeral presence keyed by roadmap, participant, and per-tab client instance. Heartbeats report visible/hidden state, active/idle interaction, current workspace section, and optional editing target; Redis TTL storage supports multi-worker deployments and memory storage supports one worker.

**Acceptance criteria**
Presence expires automatically after missed heartbeats; multiple tabs do not create misleading duplicate people; revocation removes presence immediately; presence is excluded from snapshots, versions, exports, activity history, and backups beyond operational TTL data.

**Validation / gate**
Presence service contract tests, TTL tests, privacy review, two-worker propagation test, and browser lifecycle coverage.

**Risk**
Presence can become inaccurate or invasive if persisted or over-detailed.

**Classification**
confirmed requested feature.

tasks.title: Show who is viewing, active, idle, or in a background tab
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A count alone is insufficient; users need an understandable distinction between someone actively working and someone who merely left a tab open.

**Scope**
Add a compact presence cluster and Team-panel detail showing Active now, Viewing, Idle, and Background tab states, plus connection freshness. Aggregate multiple tabs per participant while optionally exposing `2 tabs` as secondary detail.

**Acceptance criteria**
States use text and accessible labels rather than color alone; current user is identified; stale presence disappears; viewer/editor/owner visibility follows one documented privacy policy; layout works on mobile and at 200% zoom.

**Validation / gate**
Component/a11y tests, two-profile browser tests, hidden-tab/idle timers, and manual screen-reader review.

**Risk**
Ambiguous presence can be mistaken for surveillance or guaranteed attention.

**Classification**
confirmed requested feature.

tasks.title: Distinguish active editing from passive viewing
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Teams should see the difference between a roadmap being open and a collaborator actively changing a task.

**Scope**
Combine presence interaction state with lock ownership to show `Alexandre is editing this task`, current section, and recent interaction without exposing typed content or cursor positions. Keep durable claim/assignment separate from ephemeral editing state.

**Acceptance criteria**
Editing indicators appear before another user attempts a conflicting edit; they clear on release, expiry, revocation, disconnect, or task close; claim labels remain semantically distinct; background tabs never appear as actively editing unless they still hold a valid lock and the UI explains that state.

**Validation / gate**
Two-editor browser tests, lock/presence reconciliation tests, accessibility review, and privacy checks.

**Classification**
confirmed requested distinction.

tasks.title: Notify hidden tabs of unseen remote roadmap updates
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A user with RoadForge open in another tab should notice that teammates changed the roadmap.

**Scope**
Track unseen remote update events per tab. When the document is hidden or unfocused, add a red notification dot/count to the favicon and prefix the document title. Clear the badge when the tab becomes visible and the latest authoritative state is rendered or when the user explicitly acknowledges it.

**Acceptance criteria**
Only remote, successfully applied updates increment the badge; own writes, presence heartbeats, lock refreshes, duplicates, and stale events do not; favicon generation preserves the original icon, works without canvas support via fallback, and restores cleanly; title and icon updates are accessible and tested.

**Validation / gate**
Visibility/focus unit tests, Playwright multi-tab tests, favicon pixel/DOM contract tests, reload behavior, and no memory/object-URL leaks.

**Risk**
Noisy or false notifications will train users to ignore collaboration updates.

**Classification**
confirmed requested feature.

tasks.title: Coordinate same-user tabs with BroadcastChannel
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Two tabs using the same participant session currently behave as unrelated editors and can produce duplicate presence, drafts, locks, or notifications.

**Scope**
Assign a stable per-tab client ID in session storage and use `BroadcastChannel` with a storage-event fallback to coordinate active-tab leadership, draft ownership, notification clearing, logout/revocation, and duplicate connection avoidance where safe.

**Acceptance criteria**
Tabs remain independently usable but warn before conflicting same-user edits; presence aggregates correctly; revocation/logout propagates; only one tab clears another tab's unseen state through an explicit acknowledged event; unsupported browsers degrade safely.

**Validation / gate**
Multi-tab browser tests, fallback tests, crash/close recovery, and privacy review.

**Classification**
confirmed architecture gap and requested behavior.

tasks.title: Persist unsynced server-backed drafts locally
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A refresh, crash, or offline session must not destroy unsynced team work held only in React memory.

**Finding**
Current local storage tracks identity and roadmap IDs, not the active server-backed draft snapshot.

**Scope**
Store encrypted-at-rest-where-practical or origin-scoped IndexedDB drafts keyed by roadmap and participant, with base revision, pending activity, changed fields, timestamp, and schema version. Restore through an explicit recovery flow and purge after confirmed synchronization, revocation, logout, or retention expiry.

**Acceptance criteria**
Offline edits survive refresh and browser restart; stale drafts are compared with server state rather than auto-overwritten; exports never include session tokens; storage quotas/failures are surfaced; local-only roadmap behavior is unchanged.

**Validation / gate**
IndexedDB tests, crash/offline/reload browser tests, conflict recovery tests, quota simulation, and security review.

**Risk**
Persisted drafts can leak sensitive roadmap content on shared devices if retention and logout behavior are weak.

**Classification**
likely P1 data-loss prevention.

tasks.title: Make lock loss, release, and recovery explicit
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A user should never continue editing under the false belief that they still own a lock.

**Finding**
Lock expiry is passive; the previous holder is not proactively told, and browser close relies on TTL.

**Scope**
Add explicit release on editor exit where reliable, server events for lost/replaced/expired locks, refresh-failure handling, a clear draft-safe blocked state, and an owner force-release action with confirmation and attribution. Keep TTL as the crash safety net.

**Acceptance criteria**
A lost lock immediately stops autosync for that target while preserving the draft; the holder sees who owns the lock and recovery choices; normal close releases promptly; force release is owner-only and audited; no stale holder can silently overwrite.

**Validation / gate**
Lock state-machine tests, timer tests, two-editor browser tests, browser-close approximation, Redis/memory parity, and accessibility review.

**Classification**
likely P1.

tasks.title: Clarify and reconcile claim versus edit-lock behavior
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Assignment responsibility and current editing exclusivity are valid separate concepts, but users must not confuse them.

**Scope**
Document and encode the policy: claim means responsible for the task; lock means editing now. Update labels, tooltips, Team panel, task metadata, override messaging, and remote notifications. Define allowed owner claim override while another user edits without coupling claim APIs to locks.

**Acceptance criteria**
Every relevant UI names the concept explicitly; overriding a claim never implies lock takeover; the prior claimant receives a clear remote update; tests cover claim/lock combinations and role boundaries.

**Validation / gate**
State matrix, component tests, two-user browser flow, documentation review, and screen-reader labels.

**Classification**
confirmed product decision.

tasks.title: Add real multi-browser collaboration end-to-end tests
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Mocked services cannot prove that real owner/editor/viewer browsers remain coherent.

**Scope**
Create deterministic Playwright projects using a disposable API/database for save/share/join, live update, role restrictions, revocation, presence, lock contention/loss, conflict choices, restore conflict, offline draft recovery, hidden-tab notification, and same-user multi-tab behavior.

**Acceptance criteria**
Tests run in CI without production secrets; failures retain traces/screenshots/logs; no fixed sleeps hide races; owner/editor/viewer and accessibility behavior are asserted through user-visible outcomes.

**Validation / gate**
Repeated CI runs, flake budget, clean disposable teardown, and a documented local command.

**Classification**
confirmed evidence gap.

tasks.title: Prove multi-worker Redis delivery, replay, and outage recovery
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Production team collaboration cannot rely solely on mocked Redis adapters.

**Scope**
Build a disposable two-or-more-worker integration environment with Redis and PostgreSQL. Verify cross-worker update/presence/revocation/lock delivery, reconnect replay, rolling worker restart, Redis restart, sequence-gap resync, and readiness transitions.

**Acceptance criteria**
Clients connected to different workers converge; revocation is immediate; Redis loss never reports false Live; recovery requires no browser refresh; replay ordering and retention are verified; test evidence is repeatable.

**Validation / gate**
Containerized integration suite, CI or scheduled workflow, fault-injection logs, and deployment-shape documentation.

**Classification**
confirmed manual-only gap.

tasks.title: Add collaboration metrics and structured diagnostics
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Reliability cannot be managed if reconnects, gaps, conflicts, and lock contention are visible only in ad-hoc logs.

**Scope**
Add privacy-safe counters/histograms and structured logs for active SSE streams, presence entries, reconnect attempts, replay/gap resync, 409 conflicts, lock acquire/deny/loss, Redis failures, revocations, and restore conflicts. Add health/readiness detail without exposing participant names or tokens.

**Acceptance criteria**
Metrics have bounded labels; no roadmap content or credentials are logged; operators can distinguish REST health from realtime degradation; runbooks define thresholds and evidence collection.

**Validation / gate**
Metric contract tests, log-redaction tests, local scrape/check, fault-injection verification, and deployed dashboard/alert decision.

**Classification**
confirmed observability gap.

tasks.title: Publish the collaboration contract, threat model, and QA runbook
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Users, contributors, and operators need one accurate description of what live collaboration guarantees and what it does not.

**Scope**
Document roles, invites, presence states, claims versus locks, draft retention, conflict/restore choices, reconnect/replay behavior, notification badge semantics, revocation guarantees, deployment topology, privacy boundaries, failure recovery, and manual QA.

**Acceptance criteria**
Documentation matches shipped labels and tests; no Google-Docs-style claim is made; every manual/deployed gate has commands, expected results, and retained evidence; stale manual-only claims are removed or dated.

**Validation / gate**
Docs/link/copy checks, contributor walkthrough, security review, and final two-session/multi-worker manual rehearsal.

**Classification**
confirmed release requirement.

tasks.title: Freeze a collaboration-ready Beta candidate and execute stabilization
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A team-collaboration Beta claim requires reproducible security, realtime, presence, draft, accessibility, and deployment evidence.

**Scope**
Freeze an immutable candidate SHA after all implementation dependencies complete; run the complete automated, multi-browser, Redis multi-worker, accessibility, security, backup/restore, and manual collaboration matrices; fix only release-blocking regressions.

**Acceptance criteria**
No open P0/P1 collaboration defect remains; all required gates pass or a written owner decision records a bounded exception; known limitations and rollback criteria are published; the candidate SHA does not change during the evidence window.

**Validation / gate**
Release check, browser/API/integration suites, NVDA/VoiceOver, real 200% zoom/touch, two-session and multi-worker smoke, operational proof gate, and signed candidate record.

**Risk**
Late feature work invalidates collaboration evidence and can reintroduce silent divergence.

**Classification**
release-only; needs verification.

tasks.title: Publish and monitor the collaboration-ready Beta release
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A collaboration release is complete only after production rollout proves security, convergence, recovery, and rollback.

**Scope**
Publish release notes and limitations, take and verify a pre-deploy backup, deploy the immutable candidate, confirm HTTPS/security headers/proxy identity, verify two-session and Redis multi-worker collaboration, test presence and hidden-tab update badges, monitor collaboration metrics, and retain an executable rollback.

**Acceptance criteria**
Deployed SHA/tag/migrations/docs agree; revocation and restore-conflict guarantees work; reconnect/replay and presence converge across workers; no credentials appear in logs; alerts and rollback ownership are recorded; the monitoring window closes without an unresolved P0/P1 defect.

**Validation / gate**
Production smoke, backup/restore and rollback rehearsal, collaboration metric review, incident threshold check, and post-release report.

**Risk**
A locally green build cannot prove reliable actual-team collaboration.

**Classification**
release/deployment-only; needs verification.

tasks.title: Reassess identity and external API expansion from Beta evidence
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Accounts, API v1, OAuth/OIDC, personal access tokens, and service accounts change the product’s security and support model.

**Finding**
Product direction explicitly pauses platform expansion until real Beta usage evidence exists.

**Scope**
Collect usage evidence and publish a decision record before adding identity or external API work.

**Acceptance criteria**
No account/API implementation starts before Beta release review and a new threat/model ownership decision.

**Validation / gate**
Post-Beta product/security review.

**Risk**
Premature identity expansion would distract from local-first stability.

**Evidence**
Product direction in this roadmap; classification confirmed.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Reassess automation integrations from Beta evidence
tasks.desc:
**Why**
MCP, agent change sets, webhooks, GitHub metadata/sync, and billing require stable contracts and operational support.

**Finding**
These capabilities are explicitly deferred and no Beta dependency justifies them.

**Scope**
Decide whether to pursue any automation integration only after Beta workflow evidence and contract/versioning strategy.

**Acceptance criteria**
No MCP, webhooks, agent writes, GitHub sync, or billing is included in Beta scope.

**Validation / gate**
Post-Beta product/architecture review.

**Risk**
Automation can magnify data-integrity and privacy failures.

**Evidence**
Product direction in this roadmap; classification confirmed.

**Classification**
confirmed
